title: Live queue in its own chunk, so the startup bundle fits RF-201 and RF-199
acceptance: LiveWorkspace (the Live destination's queue) lives in its own file and Dashboard loads it with lazyWithReload behind a Suspense boundary, the first time Live opens.
With RF-201 on main, the startup entry is under the 180 kB gzip budget with room for RF-199, without changing the budget.
The Live queue tests and the rest of the web suite pass unchanged apart from where LiveWorkspace is imported.

evidence.summary: On main 94fc49d the entry was 179.97 kB; #746 alone made it 180.05 kB and #745 alone 180.12 kB. Owner, 2026-11-07 in the Neo session: "Yes, your plan is approved" for splitting LiveWorkspace on #746 instead of raising the budget.
LiveWorkspace split into its own lazy chunk, alongside RF-201.
pnpm --filter @ritmofit/web build on #746 merged with main: entry 178.17 kB gzip (was 180.05 kB); LiveWorkspace chunk 2.86 kB gzip. Web unit suite: 1762 tests passed.

resolution: Done on #746 (Neo, 2026-11-07). LiveWorkspace and its private helpers (the per-class payload state, its read and the queue card) moved from Dashboard.tsx to LiveWorkspace.tsx, loaded with lazyWithReload behind a Suspense boundary that shows a three-row loading skeleton. The shared Retry button class moved to SharedState.tsx so both files use one copy. The entry dropped from 180.05 to 178.17 kB gzip, leaving room for RF-199 (#745). The chunk is precached by the service worker like the other lazy chunks, so Live still opens offline; the cost is one short loading state the first time Live opens in a session.
